newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower ahead of CPI.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Sunday ahead of the release of November's consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
The CPI, announced after the close of trading, rose 0.6 percent against a rise of 0.8 percent in October.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.58 percent, or 1.20 points, to 205.69 on all-share turnover of 70 million shekels against 90 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.56 percent to 213.74.
"Activity declined today because the market was awaiting the CPI release. The market was expecting a rise of 0.5 to 0.7 percent. A higher figure would have been very dissappointing," said one trader.
"Several investors were taking profits today but the market is still very strong," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments and Securities.
"Investors were also reacting to the decision to grant financial benefits to Jewish settlers in the West Bank. This might have a negative impact on the peace process," the first trader added.
The Israeli cabinet decided on Friday to reinstate investment benefits to settlements in the West Bank after an attack in which a settler and her son were killed.
"The market is nervous as investors wait for political developments. Investors are also worried because of the instability of Wall Street," Hoffman added.
Supersol lost 0.25 percent to 7,909 after it said it is exploring acquiring the supermarket business of retailer Shekem.
Shekem surged 6.0 percent to 104.5, while Elco Holdings, Shekem's parent company, rose 3.5 percent to 8,775.

The most active shares were Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 1.0 percent to 781 on volume of 2.7 million shekels; Formula Systems, which gained 1.75 percent to 2,884 on turnover of 2.5 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 0.5 percent to 151,061 on volume of 2.4 million shekels.
Traders said Formula traded heavily in response to an announcement last week that the company planned to float shares in the United States.
